title: Verifier-Triggered Bounded Repair for LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Paired Study under Shared Initial Candidate Semantics
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset). Provider-call reconciliation records 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair (201 hosted-model calls). Baseline configurations passed the deterministic verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline (verifier allowed ≤1 repair) passed 200/200 (100%). Contingency counts: n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact two-sided McNemar p (exact-binomial convention) = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a required-sequence ordering violation in an extreme multi-step task. We report the preregistration, full execution accounting (start 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00, end 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00, elapsed ≈29 minutes), deterministic reconciliation, representative diagnostic traces for the repaired pair (task-000008), and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction: LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into low-level device configuration artifacts for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness for such workflows requires generated configurations to satisfy deterministic invariants (ordering constraints, group-level safety, reachability, policy compliance). Prior prototype systems and benchmarks demonstrate feasibility for intent→configuration workflows but leave an empirical gap: when the exact same initial generated candidate is reused across comparison conditions, what is the marginal effect of permitting a verifier-triggered bounded repair? This paper answers that narrower question using a preregistered paired design in which baseline and guarded episodes share the identical initial candidate per task (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). Under these semantics any paired difference can only arise from deterministic validation and the single allowed repair; it cannot arise from independent guarded first-pass generations, prompt engineering, or selection among multiple samples. We therefore measure a repair-only estimand: the paired difference in per-task binary acceptance by a deterministic verifier.
sections.related_work: Work on LLM-assisted NetOps has focused on end-to-end intent→config prototypes and benchmark-style evaluations that motivate verifier-aware pipelines [1,39,40]. Deterministic configuration verification methods (symbolic or rule-based verifiers) provide operational oracles appropriate for syntactic and ordered-workflow invariants and have been used as the natural scoring mechanism in configuration-synthesis evaluations [2,85]. In adjacent domains, generate→validate→repair and test-in-the-loop program-repair pipelines show that validating generated artifacts against executable oracles and applying bounded repairs can produce correct artifacts [Li 2024 et al.]. However, most such demonstrations are in software engineering or scientific-model domains rather than NetOps-specific, multi-device sequencing contexts; the literature therefore supports the proposal and engineering demonstration of verifier-mediated repair but does not by itself quantify repair-only effects for network-configuration ordering or group-level invariants. Tool-augmented agent architectures and RAG/MCP-style designs further motivate coupling generators to specialized solvers and validators, while reporting and preregistration guidelines emphasize artifacted reporting for confirmatory LLM studies [3,6]. Our paired, shared_initial_candidate experiment addresses the specific empirical gap of quantifying the marginal repair effect when identical initial candidates are deterministically reused across baseline and guarded conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as CAND-2026-001 and fixed a paired binary estimand: per-task difference in deterministic-verifier acceptance (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Key preregistered design choices included N=200 tasks, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by baseline and guarded), a maximum of one automated repair call per task, primary failed-call handling complete_pair_primary, and confirmatory testing via the exact two-sided McNemar test plus a paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The execution manifest and analysis artifacts are archived and reproduce the reported counts and intervals.

Deterministic tasks and verifier oracle. Tasks were produced by a deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (an ordered list of required field/interface updates), allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies. The deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parsers commands, enforces allowed_fields and required_sequence ordering, evaluates group-level invariants (final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups), and returns full_intent_constraint_validation only when all encoded constraints are satisfied. The verifier emits structured tracer outputs (validation_before, validation_after, violation_codes) that serve as the authoritative evidence for per-episode scoring.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and sampling notes. The adapter contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair the identical single initial generation (shared_initial_candidate) was used by both baseline and guarded episodes. This design isolates a repair-only estimand: any observed paired difference must originate from the verifier and the single permitted repair. The model-configuration record declares requested_model = gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null (unset); per preregistration and artifact rules we explicitly note that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The experiment used one initial sample per task by design; nondeterministic hosted-model sampling may remain a background property but did not produce additional independent samples under shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Pipeline, sanitizer, and bounded repair. For each task the pipeline ran a deterministic formatting sanitizer, then submitted the sanitized prompt to the hosted model to produce the shared initial candidate. If the verifier reported invariant violations, the guarded logic could invoke at most one automated repair call to the hosted model using a repair prompt constructed from the verifier trace (as preregistered). Repair calls were counted against the maximum_model_calls budget; the deterministic reconciliation records shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1, summing to hosted_model_call_event_count = 201. Persistent unparsables after sanitizer and the permitted repair were handled per the preregistered missingness plan; none occurred in this run.

Statistical procedures. The primary confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar test computed from discordant counts n10 and n01. We implemented the exact two-sided p-value using the exact binomial-tail convention described in the preregistration; with n = n10 + n01 and k = n10, p = 2 × min{BinomCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 − BinomCDF(k − 1; n, 0.5)} (conventional handling when k = 0). For the paired absolute risk difference we computed a paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI with 10,000 resamples using seed 1729; bootstrap parameters are recorded in the archived analysis log. Planned power targeted detection of ~10–15 percentage-point paired improvements at N=200 under mid-range baseline assumptions (~45–65%), but the realized baseline rate differed (see Results), which affects realized sensitivity.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and audit. The run completed without preregistered exclusions. Execution manifest timestamps show start 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00 and end 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00 (elapsed ≈29 minutes). Planned_episode_count = 400 and completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call reconciliation and deterministic_reconciliation record hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1} and cache_miss_count = 201 (cache_hit_count = 0), matching the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and a single repair invocation.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Analysis artifacts report baseline_success_count = 199 and guarded_success_count = 200 (complete_pairs = 200). The paired contingency table is n11 = 199, n10 = 1 (guarded success, baseline failure), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. With n = n10 + n01 = 1 and k = n10 = 1 the exact two-sided McNemar p-value (exact-binomial convention) equals p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.00, 0.015]. These numeric artifacts reproduce when the archived analysis executor is re-run on the recorded raw results.

Single repair event and diagnostic trace. The guarded pipeline invoked exactly one automated repair. The repaired pair is archived and identified as task-000008 in the representative_task set. That task’s manifest encodes difficulty metadata: changed_interface_count = 3, dependency_rule_count = 4, required_command_count = 9, difficulty.level = "extreme". The verifier tracer documents validation_before.violation_codes indicating a required_sequence ordering breach: the shared initial candidate performed the uplink1 MTU change before the uplink1 VLAN change, violating the task's required_sequence (vlan before mtu). The guarded repair prompt (constructed from the validator trace) produced a repaired candidate whose validation_after.valid = true; the scorer returned score = 1 with scorer_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION". These per-episode tracer fields constitute the archived evidence that the single observed paired improvement resulted from a verifier-triggered repair that corrected an ordering/dependency violation expressible in the task manifest.

Representative diagnostics and difficulty composition. Representative task manifests in the archived bundle span required_command_count = 3–9 and changed_interface_count up to 3 in the sampled subset. The lone baseline failure (the discordant pair) is associated with the extreme composite difficulty profile above; exploratory diagnostics in the archive are consistent with the preregistered hypothesis that multi-device sequencing and higher required_command_count concentrate residual failures.

Missingness, exclusions, and reconciliation. The run recorded no preregistered exclusions and no persistent unparsables; missingness_summary reports complete_pairs = 200 and zeros for other missingness categories. Deterministic_reconciliation indicates pair_accounting_consistent = true and all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true.
sections.discussion:
What the paired shared_initial_candidate estimand measures. Because baseline and guarded episodes reused the exact same sampled candidate per task, the paired difference isolates the marginal effect of permitting a single verifier-triggered repair. The measured estimand therefore quantifies a repair-only effect: it does not measure benefits that would accrue from independent guarded first-pass generations, prompt-template differences, multi-sample selection, or alternative guarded-generation semantics. Any operational interpretation must therefore be constrained to repair-mediated changes applied to an otherwise identical initial candidate.

Statistical regime and interpretation. The realized baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) placed the confirmatory test in a sparse-discordant regime (only one discordant pair). In such regimes the exact two-sided McNemar p-value provides limited directional evidence (here p = 1.0 under the exact-binomial convention for n = 1, k = 1). The paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI [0.00, 0.015] quantifies compatible absolute improvements attributable to repair under this repair-only estimand: the data are consistent with at most small absolute gains (upper bound 0.015) in this specific setting. The preregistered power rationale (targeting detectability of ~10–15 percentage points at N=200 under mid-range baseline assumptions) was not realized because baseline performance was much higher than planned; consequently realized inferential sensitivity for modest repair-only effects is limited.

Failure-mode analysis grounded in artifacts. The archived validator traces show that the repaired failure was an ordering violation (required_sequence breach) detectable by the deterministic verifier and correctable by a bounded textual repair that reordered the explicit configuration commands. This failure mode is operationally interpretable: when required sequence constraints are encoded in the task manifest and the verifier exposes the ordering failure in its trace, a bounded generator repair can produce a syntactic/ordering correction accepted by the verifier. Conversely, the evidence does not support repair efficacy for faults unexpressible in the verifier’s invariant set (e.g., dataplane-only anomalies or vendor runtime behaviors not captured by the verifier's encoded constraints).

Limitations of scope and external validity. Internal validity: the paired shared_initial_candidate design isolates repair effects but leaves prompt sensitivity and model-sampling variability untested. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded syntactic, ordering, and group-level invariants but is not a substitute for dataplane emulation or vendor-specific runtime semantics. External validity: the study used one hosted model (declared gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank focused on very_hard/extreme patterns; generalization across models, richer topologies, vendor templates, or live devices is untested. Adversarial or contaminated-context attacks were not included in this run; resilience to poisoned retrievals or adversarial prompts remains an open empirical question. Practical implication: artifact-grounded evidence supports the constrained claim that a verifier-triggered bounded repair corrected a localized ordering fault in one extreme synthetic task under these verifier-backstopped conditions. Broader operational claims (reduced triage time, deployment safety improvements on live networks) were not measured here and require further empirical evaluation.

Concrete follow-up evaluation axes (supported by the archived design space). The archived artifacts and unresolved questions motivate: (1) multi-model replication to assess generality across generator families; (2) experiments that lift shared_initial_candidate semantics to allow independent guarded first-pass generations or multi-sample selection to quantify generator+selection effects versus repair-only effects; (3) adversarial/poisoning studies that introduce contaminated retrievals or malicious context to evaluate guardrail robustness; and (4) live-device or dataplane-emulation experiments to link verifier-checked invariants to runtime correctness. These follow-ups are distinct experiments and are proposed as next steps rather than claimed outcomes of the present run.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) that measured the marginal effect of permitting a single verifier-triggered bounded repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In 200 deterministic synthetic tasks with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; provider-call reconciliation records 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair (201 model calls total). The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. The single observed improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a required-sequence ordering violation in an extreme multi-step task (task-000008). Artifact-grounded evidence therefore supports a constrained conclusion: when ordering and workflow invariants are encoded in a deterministic verifier and exposed via structured traces, a bounded verifier-guided repair can correct localized ordering faults in generated configurations. Broader operational claims require additional, specifically designed experiments (multi-model studies, independent-guarded-generation contrasts, adversarial contamination testing, and live-device/dataplane emulation). The preregistration, deterministic reconciliation, raw artifacts, and analysis executor are archived for audit and reanalysis.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Deterministic verifier (oracle): deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Archived provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are available in the execution bundle for audit.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts or multi-sample selection.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
